speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a recent low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any joint pain or swollen lymph nodes recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet Fever (or similar exanthematous illness) - based on the classic "sandpaper-like" rash description, fever, rhinorrhea, and headache in an 11-year-old, though the "sparing the perioral area" detail is atypical for Scarlet Fever and may suggest Kawasaki disease, Rubella, or Measles. Please confirm if she has had any recent sore throat or if the rash feels like sandpaper.
